<!--
  WADE setup. Paste this chunk into the v8 setup region (after the cohort-set
  chunk that defines `cds`/`mats`, and after the sources for
  R/control_strata.R, R/group_structure.R, wade.R, R/wade_contrasts.R and
  R/wade_figures.R). It computes every object the §4.x WADE section and the S7
  supplement quote, so nothing in either fragment is inline-computed twice and
  nothing is hardcoded.

  Add to the source block:
    source(cfrna_here("R/control_strata.R"))   # control taxonomy (registry-driven)
    source(cfrna_here("R/group_structure.R"))  # PCA of the analysis matrix
    source(cfrna_here("wade.R"))               # the statistic
    source(cfrna_here("R/wade_contrasts.R"))   # contrast registry + screen + cache
    source(cfrna_here("R/wade_figures.R"))     # WADE figure grammar
-->

```{r}
#| label: wade-setup
#| include: false
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cohorts. Both definitions are carried through every contrast; the section
# reports the main one and the cohort-comparison table covers both. Named
# rather than positional so a reordered checkpoint cannot silently swap them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_cds  <- cds
wade_mats <- mats
WADE_COHORT_MAIN <- "all panels"
stopifnot(WADE_COHORT_MAIN %in% names(wade_cds))

# The primary detection contrast, and the genes the diagnostic figure draws.
# Named here (not inside the figure call) so the section and the figure cannot
# disagree about which contrast is primary.
WADE_PRIMARY <- "cancer_vs_hr"
WADE_NPERMS  <- CFRNA_WADE_NPERMS

# Canonical markers always labelled on the volcano regardless of rank, so a
# reader can locate familiar genes. Not a nomination claim.
WADE_CANON_GENES <- c("CEACAM5", "MUC1", "AGR2", "SERPINB5", "KRT19")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Registry audit. Runs FIRST and with strict = TRUE: if a future store adds a
# control-like disease that no stratum names, the build stops here rather than
# counting those patients as cancer cases. That failure is exactly what
# `prostate_high_psa` did silently before this module existed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_audit <- cfrna_control_strata_audit(
  wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$libraries$disease, strict = TRUE)

# Stratum composition per cohort, for the §4.x.1 table.
wade_strata <- lapply(wade_cds, function(cd) cfrna_strata_summary(cd$libraries))

# Scalars the §4.x.1 callout quotes. Both are the SIZE of a misclassification
# that has actually occurred in this project, so they are computed from the
# cohort rather than typed.
wade_lb_main <- wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$libraries
wade_n_hr  <- sum(wade_lb_main$disease %in% CFRNA_CONTROL_STRATA$hr_surveil)
wade_n_psa <- dplyr::n_distinct(
  wade_lb_main$patient[wade_lb_main$disease == "prostate_high_psa"])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exchangeability. The measurement behind every patient-level caveat: are
# libraries independent? Quoted in §4.x.2.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_exch <- cfrna_gs_exchangeability(wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]],
                                     wade_mats[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contrast screen, per cohort. Cheap (no permutations), so it is computed
# rather than cached.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_screen <- lapply(wade_cds, function(cd) cfrna_wade_screen(cd$libraries))

# Which contrasts run, and which may contribute nominations. `tail_ok` is read
# off the screen rather than decided at each figure call, so one threshold
# governs the volcano, the nomination table and the CSV exports.
wade_runnable <- lapply(wade_screen, function(s) unique(cfrna_wade_runnable(s)$id))
wade_tail_ok  <- local({
  s <- dplyr::filter(wade_screen[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]], unit == "index")
  setNames(as.list(s$tail_usable), s$id)
})
wade_nominatable <- local({
  s <- dplyr::filter(wade_screen[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]], unit == "index")
  s$id[s$nominatable]
})

# Screen scalars quoted in §4.x.2 prose.
wade_v_screenpos <- local({
  s <- dplyr::filter(wade_screen[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]], unit == "index",
                     id == "screenpos_vs_hr")
  s$panel_v[1]
})
# What restricting the refused contrast to one design version would give -- the
# number that turns "refused" into a specific enrolment target.
wade_pm_v6_nctrl <- local({
  sp <- CFRNA_WADE_CONTRASTS[[which(vapply(CFRNA_WADE_CONTRASTS,
                                          function(x) x$id, character(1)) == "screenpos_vs_hr")]]
  pm <- cfrna_wade_panel_matched(wade_lb_main, sp)
  pm$n_ctrl[pm$design == "v6"]
})

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run WADE. Cached per contrast per cohort -- the cache key covers the store
# fingerprint, cohort name, gene count and both groups' library ids, so a
# refresh invalidates rather than silently reusing. First build is ~25 min for
# both cohorts; a re-render reloads in seconds.
#
# The (count, normalizer) pair is rigel TOTAL counts over effective length,
# giving standard TPM. Rigel deconvolutes gDNA upstream, so total counts are
# trustworthy here and use every read rather than only the spliced fraction.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_z    <- cfrna_store(cohort)
wade_qnt  <- read_rigel_quant(wade_z, measures = c("count", "effective_length"))
wade_res  <- lapply(names(wade_cds), function(ch)
  cfrna_wade_run_all(wade_qnt$count, wade_qnt$effective_length,
                     wade_cds[[ch]], wade_runnable[[ch]],
                     cache_dir = cfrna_cache("wade")))
names(wade_res) <- names(wade_cds)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting objects.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_sig <- lapply(wade_res, cfrna_wade_signal_check)

# Cross-contrast membership uses only the NOMINATABLE contrasts: a descriptive
# contrast is run and reported, but it does not contribute nominations, so
# including it here would let a 5-patient comparison mark a gene as consensus.
wade_cross <- lapply(names(wade_res), function(ch) {
  keep <- intersect(names(wade_res[[ch]]), wade_nominatable)
  cfrna_wade_cross(wade_res[[ch]][keep], top_n = 100L,
                   tail_ok = all(unlist(wade_tail_ok[keep])))
})
names(wade_cross) <- names(wade_res)

# Per-gene diagnostic inputs: the normalized matrix WADE actually ran on for
# the primary contrast, rebuilt with the same seed so the curves are the same
# numbers the statistic saw.
wade_primary_libs <- cfrna_wade_resolve(
  CFRNA_WADE_CONTRASTS[[which(vapply(CFRNA_WADE_CONTRASTS,
                                     function(x) x$id, character(1)) == WADE_PRIMARY)]],
  wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$libraries)
wade_libs <- c(wade_primary_libs$case, wade_primary_libs$ctrl)
wade_cond <- c(rep(1L, length(wade_primary_libs$case)),
               rep(0L, length(wade_primary_libs$ctrl)))
wade_gi   <- wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$gene_idx
wade_Xc   <- wade_qnt$count[wade_gi, wade_libs, drop = FALSE]
wade_Xn   <- wade_qnt$effective_length[wade_gi, wade_libs, drop = FALSE]
wade_tpm  <- wade_normalize(wade_Xc, wade_Xn,
                            wade_lib_size(wade_Xc, wade_Xn), seed = 1L)
rownames(wade_tpm) <- wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$gene_name

# Four genes spanning the profiles the diagnostic is built to distinguish,
# CHOSEN FROM THE DATA rather than carried over from v7 -- v7's picks
# (CEACAM5 / MUC1 / PANTR1 / GRM7) were right for v7's contrast and cohort and
# may not be the illustrative cases here.
#
# Selection rule on the primary contrast:
#   subset  top-ranked gene with tail.conc >= 0.6 AND elevated in several
#           patients -- "subset" must mean a SUBSET, so the patient count is
#           part of the definition rather than a hope about tail.conc.
#   bulk    top-ranked gene with tail.conc < 0.4.
#   outlier high tail.conc that the permutation test REFUSES, and verified to
#           exceed the control maximum in <= 2 PATIENTS. v7 asserted this
#           profile; here it is checked, because "single outlier" is the whole
#           point of the panel and a gene elevated in 19 patients would make
#           the caption false.
#   null    smallest |diff.mean| among genes whose tail.conc is INTERPRETABLE.
#           Selecting on |diff.mean| alone lands on a gene whose tail.conc has
#           exploded (the denominator is what is near zero), which prints a
#           meaningless 149 in the panel subtitle.
WADE_CURVE_GENES <- local({
  r  <- wade_res[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]][[WADE_PRIMARY]]
  # Patients above the control maximum, per gene -- the measurement that makes
  # "subset" and "single outlier" claims checkable rather than asserted.
  lbp <- wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$libraries
  pat <- lbp$patient[match(colnames(wade_tpm), lbp$library)]
  n_pat_above <- function(g) {
    v <- wade_tpm[g, ]; mx <- max(v[wade_cond == 0])
    dplyr::n_distinct(pat[wade_cond == 1 & v > mx])
  }
  d <- dplyr::filter(r, diff.mean > 0, !is.na(tail.conc), abs(tail.conc) <= 1.5)

  cand_sub <- d |> dplyr::filter(tail.conc >= 0.6) |> dplyr::arrange(rank)
  g_sub <- cand_sub$gene[which(vapply(cand_sub$gene, n_pat_above, integer(1)) >= 5)[1]]

  g_bulk <- d |> dplyr::filter(tail.conc < 0.4) |> dplyr::arrange(rank) |>
    dplyr::slice(1) |> dplyr::pull(gene)

  cand_out <- d |> dplyr::filter(p.tail > 0.5, tail.conc > 0.9) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(diff.mean))
  g_out <- cand_out$gene[which(vapply(cand_out$gene, n_pat_above, integer(1)) <= 2)[1]]

  g_null <- d |> dplyr::arrange(abs(diff.mean)) |> dplyr::slice(1) |> dplyr::pull(gene)
  unique(c(g_sub, g_bulk, g_out, g_null))
})
# Patient counts for the caption, so the figure's own claims are computed.
WADE_CURVE_NPAT <- local({
  lbp <- wade_cds[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]$libraries
  pat <- lbp$patient[match(colnames(wade_tpm), lbp$library)]
  vapply(WADE_CURVE_GENES, function(g) {
    v <- wade_tpm[g, ]; mx <- max(v[wade_cond == 0])
    dplyr::n_distinct(pat[wade_cond == 1 & v > mx])
  }, integer(1))
})
WADE_CURVE_TITLES <- setNames(
  paste0(WADE_CURVE_GENES, c("  (subset marker)", "  (bulk shift)",
                             "  (single outlier \u2014 test refuses)",
                             "  (null)")[seq_along(WADE_CURVE_GENES)]),
  WADE_CURVE_GENES)

# Nomination table for the primary contrast, with cross-contrast support.
wade_nom_table <- lapply(names(wade_res), function(ch) {
  r  <- cfrna_wade_nominate(wade_res[[ch]][[WADE_PRIMARY]],
                            tail_ok = isTRUE(wade_tail_ok[[WADE_PRIMARY]]))
  cx <- wade_cross[[ch]]
  n_other <- cx$n_nominating[match(r$gene, cx$gene)] - 1L
  r |>
    dplyr::mutate(n_other = ifelse(is.na(n_other), 0L, pmax(n_other, 0L))) |>
    dplyr::arrange(rank) |> dplyr::slice(1:25) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Rank = rank, Gene = gene,
                     `diff.mean` = round(diff.mean, 0),
                     fc = round(fc, 1),
                     `tail.conc` = round(tail.conc, 2),
                     `p.diff` = signif(p.diff, 2),
                     `other contrasts` = n_other)
})
names(wade_nom_table) <- names(wade_res)

# Cohort comparison. `measurable` is the denominator that makes `shared`
# readable: a nomination absent from the other cohort may be a gene that cohort
# cannot measure rather than a disagreement.
wade_cohort_compare <- local({
  chs <- names(wade_res)
  ids <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(wade_res, names))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(id) {
    sets <- lapply(chs, function(ch) {
      r <- cfrna_wade_nominate(wade_res[[ch]][[id]],
                               tail_ok = isTRUE(wade_tail_ok[[id]]))
      r$gene[r$nominated]
    })
    names(sets) <- chs
    genes <- lapply(chs, function(ch) wade_cds[[ch]]$gene_name)
    names(genes) <- chs
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(chs, function(ch) {
      other <- setdiff(chs, ch)[1]
      tibble::tibble(
        Contrast = attr(wade_res[[ch]][[id]], "contrast_label"),
        Cohort = ch, Genes = length(genes[[ch]]),
        nominated = length(sets[[ch]]),
        measurable = sum(sets[[other]] %in% genes[[ch]]),
        shared = length(intersect(sets[[ch]], sets[[other]])))
    }))
  }))
})

# Cost table for S7.7. `cached` distinguishes a fresh run from a reload, so the
# quoted timing is honest about which it is.
wade_cost <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(wade_res), function(ch)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(wade_res[[ch]]), function(id) {
    r <- wade_res[[ch]][[id]]
    tibble::tibble(Contrast = attr(r, "contrast_label"), Cohort = ch,
                   Genes = attr(r, "n_genes"),
                   `Case/Ctrl` = sprintf("%d / %d", attr(r, "n_case"), attr(r, "n_ctrl")),
                   `Seconds` = round(attr(r, "elapsed_sec") %||% NA_real_, 1))
  }))))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The combinatorial permutation floor (S7.4): probability that label shuffling
# puts all k altered samples in the case group. A property of the group sizes
# alone, so it is computed exactly rather than simulated -- v7 simulated the
# equivalent curve, which was slower and noisier for the same answer.
#
# DEFINED IN SETUP, NOT IN THE SUPPLEMENT CHUNK. The prose quotes these values
# ABOVE the chunk that used to build them, and an inline `r` on a not-yet-
# defined object renders as an EMPTY STRING rather than erroring -- the exact
# silent failure gate 6 exists to catch. Anything quoted anywhere is built here.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_pfloor <- function(n1, n0, k) exp(lchoose(n1, k) - lchoose(n1 + n0, k))
wade_floor_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(wade_res[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]]), function(id) {
  r  <- wade_res[[WADE_COHORT_MAIN]][[id]]
  n1 <- attr(r, "n_case"); n0 <- attr(r, "n_ctrl")
  tibble::tibble(id = id, n_case = n1, n_ctrl = n0,
                 k2 = wade_pfloor(n1, n0, 2), k3 = wade_pfloor(n1, n0, 3),
                 k5 = wade_pfloor(n1, n0, 5))
}))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The single FDR-significant result across every run, and the evidence that it
# is a GPD extrapolation artefact rather than a discovery (S7.4 callout).
# Found by SEARCHING all runs rather than by knowing which one it is, so if a
# future refresh moves it -- or produces none -- the callout tracks the data.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
wade_n_runs <- sum(vapply(wade_res, length, integer(1)))
wade_gpd <- local({
  fl <- 1 / (WADE_NPERMS * 250)          # the .gpd_tail_p() floor
  hits <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(wade_res), function(ch)
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(wade_res[[ch]]), function(id) {
      r <- wade_res[[ch]][[id]]
      s <- dplyr::filter(r, padj.tail < 0.10 | padj.diff < 0.10)
      if (!nrow(s)) return(NULL)
      dplyr::transmute(s, cohort = ch, id = id, gene,
                       p = pmin(p.tail, p.diff),
                       padj = pmin(padj.tail, padj.diff),
                       at_floor = p <= fl,
                       n_genes = nrow(r),
                       n_case = attr(r, "n_case"), n_ctrl = attr(r, "n_ctrl"))
    }))))
  stopifnot(nrow(hits) >= 1)             # the callout describes a real hit
  dplyr::arrange(hits, padj)[1, ]
})
wade_gpd_gene   <- wade_gpd$gene
wade_gpd_padj   <- wade_gpd$padj
wade_gpd_p      <- wade_gpd$p
wade_gpd_ngenes <- wade_gpd$n_genes
wade_gpd_nprobs <- min(wade_gpd$n_case, wade_gpd$n_ctrl)
# What BH would give from the EMPIRICAL floor alone -- the counterfactual that
# shows the significance is entirely the tail fit's doing.
wade_gpd_padj_emp <- (1 / (WADE_NPERMS + 1)) * wade_gpd_ngenes
# How many patients actually carry the signal.
wade_gpd_support <- local({
  cd <- wade_cds[[wade_gpd$cohort]]
  sp <- CFRNA_WADE_CONTRASTS[[which(vapply(CFRNA_WADE_CONTRASTS,
                                          function(x) x$id, character(1)) == wade_gpd$id)]]
  rr <- cfrna_wade_resolve(sp, cd$libraries)
  lbs <- c(rr$case, rr$ctrl)
  cnd <- c(rep(1L, length(rr$case)), rep(0L, length(rr$ctrl)))
  Xc <- wade_qnt$count[cd$gene_idx, lbs, drop = FALSE]
  Xn <- wade_qnt$effective_length[cd$gene_idx, lbs, drop = FALSE]
  tp <- wade_normalize(Xc, Xn, wade_lib_size(Xc, Xn), seed = 1L)
  rownames(tp) <- cd$gene_name
  v  <- tp[wade_gpd_gene, ]
  mx <- max(v[cnd == 0])
  hi <- names(v)[cnd == 1 & v > mx]
  list(n_lib = length(hi),
       n_pat = dplyr::n_distinct(cd$libraries$patient[match(hi, cd$libraries$library)]))
})
wade_gpd_nlib <- wade_gpd_support$n_lib
wade_gpd_npat <- wade_gpd_support$n_pat

# Normalizer comparison quoted in S7.6. WADE normalizes internally rather than
# consuming cfrna_cd_matrix(), so the claim "the two correct comparably" has to
# carry its own measurement. Residual dependence of per-library MEAN ABUNDANCE
# on sequencing depth after normalizing -- the same criterion R/normalize.R used
# to choose ic_spl_sum, so the two numbers are comparable.
wade_norm_rho <- local({
  f <- function(ch) {
    cd <- wade_cds[[ch]]; libs <- cd$library_ids
    Cc <- wade_qnt$count[cd$gene_idx, libs, drop = FALSE]
    Ce <- wade_qnt$effective_length[cd$gene_idx, libs, drop = FALSE]
    dep <- cd$libraries$on_spliced[match(libs, cd$libraries$library)]
    tp  <- wade_normalize(Cc, Ce, wade_lib_size(Cc, Ce), seed = 1L)
    c(raw  = stats::cor(colMeans(log2(Cc + 1)), dep, method = "spearman"),
      wade = stats::cor(colMeans(log2(tp + 1)), dep, method = "spearman"),
      proj = stats::cor(colMeans(wade_mats[[ch]][, libs, drop = FALSE]), dep,
                        method = "spearman"))
  }
  a <- f(WADE_COHORT_MAIN)
  list(raw_full = a[["raw"]], wade_full = a[["wade"]], proj_full = a[["proj"]])
})
```
